title: APIM to AI Gateway mapping rules
description: Source shape to target capability, with the verdict and how the question is answered when the mapping is not direct. Whether a rule can ever be selected is a question for `migrate-apim compile`, which checks each one against the planner's registered selection sites; this schema only decides whether the rule is well formed. `additionalProperties` is false throughout on purpose: an invented key is how a rule comes to match nothing while reading as though it matches something.

targetCapabilities.description: The catalog these rules are versioned with, by filename stem.

verdict.description: native: direct equivalent. partial: a decision is needed. gap: no target. handled: carried by another object. notApplicable: nothing to carry.

answer.description: How the question this rule raises is answered: `choose` one of `options`, or `supply` the data the decision carries -- a model list, a name per member. It replaces `itemKind`, whose seven values conflated that mechanical distinction with a presentation label: six of them meant "pick one of options" and differed only in what they were called, while the planner reads `decision.models` off exactly one kind of answer.

predicate.description: One `where` predicate, in one of exactly three forms: a value is equals, an array is one of, and {"present": bool} is non-empty or empty. Closed on purpose. `derived` was a second block of predicates and all five of its keys turned out to be tests on a real field -- `policiesBypassed: true` was `policiesApplied is False` misfiled and inverted in the name -- so folding them in is only an improvement while `where` stays small. A predicate needing `contains`, `gt` or `matches` belongs in code, where it can say why.

options.description: The choices offered when a verdict is partial. A bare string is the choice itself; the object form carries what choosing it costs.

partialWhen.description: What makes this mapping lossy for one element. Any one condition that holds demotes the rule to partial and overlays `partial` on it; requiring all of them would let an element that trips a single condition read as cleanly mapped. Each condition is named by `plan._apply_partial_when`, and a key it does not know would never fire while reading as though it did, so the set is closed here. The booleans take `true` only, for the same reason: there is no condition that holds by an element lacking an expression.

attributeIsExpression.description: The attribute whose value is a policy expression rather than a literal.

hasExpression.description: The element evaluates a policy expression anywhere in it.

underConditional.description: A `choose` branch in the source decides whether the element runs at all.

partialOverlay.description: The rule as it reads once `partialWhen` holds, overlaid on the rule itself. The verdict is already partial by then, so it is not restated here.

selects.description: Where the object this rule judges lives, as a path into the inventory, with `[]` for "each of these". One asset raises several questions and they are decided separately, so they are several paths: an API's published surface, the dialect it translates, its model catalogue and its alias names are four objects, not one.

where.description: Field predicates on the object `selects` points at. `selects` plus the key is the path `compile` checks against inventory.schema.json.

selects.description: Where the object this rule judges lives. A fragment is selected as `apim.policyFragments[]`, the APIM resource, rather than as a policy document narrowed by `scope.level`.

disposition.description: What this migration makes of the fragment. The one predicate here that no record carries: `plan._policy_fragments` works it out, and the selection site says so, because a fragment the target must dissolve is not a fragment nothing includes, and neither is an `include-fragment` naming one this inventory does not hold.

prerequisiteWhen.description: The options that leave a manual prerequisite outstanding. Any option not named here needs nothing, so settling on it withdraws the prerequisite.

fallback.description: Answers for whatever the passes above it did not, and is tried last. There is exactly one per subject; a second is a tie `compile` rejects. It exists so an element no rule recognises still reaches the plan rather than being dropped where it was classified. Written as a flag and not as a predicate, because matching everything is not a statement about the element.

name.description: Element names, compared against `policies[].elements[].name`. The one-of form of a predicate.

expressionIds.description: `{"present": true}` is the element evaluating a policy expression anywhere in it. It was `derived.hasExpression`, a computed key that named no field; `expressionIds` is the field the collector writes.
